notes: NO PLANNED TRADES. 'I can't in good conscience assign planned trades after a session like Thursday's… Right now, the setups are trash. There is no reason to manufacture trades simply because the market is moving. Keep it small, keep it smart, and let's make it to the weekend in one piece.' He suggests Friday is a good day to reread the Starter Kit.
bias: 'The trapdoor finally opens, forced liquidation accelerates, and the ingredients for a meaningful swing low begin to emerge — but sellers remain firmly in control.' Another gap higher sold: his 7:01 AM references 'for all the marbles' — ES 7388-7396, NQ 27588-27622 — both failed; ES showed nothing above its OR5 high, NQ wicked above its overnight high and LAAF'd; Wednesday's ES box broke to the downside ('box is box') and the longstanding trapdoor setup completed — and substantially exceeded — its objective. NQ took Tuesday's low. Forced liquidation is now visible (NAAIM in the low 50s, lowest in ~18 months); the question is 'when is the last seller finished selling?' — when that happens 'the subsequent rally could be ferocious.' This is emphatically NOT a bottom call; sellers remain in complete control. He started longs Thursday against remaining puts ('I recognize that I'm early… it would still be smarter to wait'); he is done being swing short — flat or long from here, with short runners stabilizing P&L. 'The index is still objectively a short.'
wildcard: No graded setups — both sides carry extraordinary risk (longs: further forced liquidation; shorts: violent reversal on exhaustion). He is unlikely to add shorts below Thursday's low and has 'no interest in initiating shorts into' the NQ HTF references. KOSPI 4890: a gap-lower sweep that gets bought would be one of the better signs of a developing local low; persistent weakness below it adds pressure. ES 7043-7232 is his broad zone for a partial prior-ATH backtest; the overnight low after the letter reached just below 7169-7170 (top of the April-breakout demand distribution — 'demand can matter very little in the middle of a broad liquidation').
